variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: NGINX is an event-driven web server and traffic proxy. It can accept a client connection, terminate TLS, select a virtual server and location, enforce request limits, serve a local or cached response, or proxy the request to an upstream application.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Web server
pairs.detail: Serve static files, redirects, errors, health endpoints, or generated module responses without opening an upstream connection.
pairs.explanation: Serve static files, redirects, errors, health endpoints, or generated module responses without opening an upstream connection.

pairs.label: Reverse proxy
pairs.detail: Normalize the request boundary, select an upstream, apply deadlines and buffering, and return a controlled response.
pairs.explanation: Normalize the request boundary, select an upstream, apply deadlines and buffering, and return a controlled response.

pairs.label: Load balancer
pairs.detail: Choose among upstream servers with round robin, least connections, hashing, weights, and passive or configured health behavior.
pairs.explanation: Choose among upstream servers with round robin, least connections, hashing, weights, and passive or configured health behavior.

pairs.label: HTTP cache
pairs.detail: Store reusable responses under an explicit identity and freshness policy, then serve a hit or permitted stale response without contacting the origin.
pairs.explanation: Store reusable responses under an explicit identity and freshness policy, then serve a hit or permitted stale response without contacting the origin.

variants.hint:
Web server: Serve static files, redirects, errors, health endpoints, or generated module responses without opening an upstream connection.

Reverse proxy: Normalize the request boundary, select an upstream, apply deadlines and buffering, and return a controlled response.

Load balancer: Choose among upstream servers with round robin, least connections, hashing, weights, and passive or configured health behavior.

HTTP cache: Store reusable responses under an explicit identity and freshness policy, then serve a hit or permitted stale response without contacting the origin.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Master process
pairs.detail: Validate and load configuration, own privileged startup work, and coordinate reload, reopen, quit, and worker replacement signals.
pairs.explanation: Validate and load configuration, own privileged startup work, and coordinate reload, reopen, quit, and worker replacement signals.

pairs.label: Worker event loop
pairs.detail: One worker can manage many sockets with non-blocking I/O.
pairs.explanation: One worker can manage many sockets with non-blocking I/O. Slow network clients do not require one operating-system thread each.

pairs.label: Shared zones
pairs.detail: Rate-limit state, cache metadata, upstream state, and other module data may live in explicitly sized shared-memory zones.
pairs.explanation: Rate-limit state, cache metadata, upstream state, and other module data may live in explicitly sized shared-memory zones.

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Round robin
pairs.detail: Rotate requests across available servers.
pairs.explanation: Rotate requests across available servers. It is a clear baseline when instances and request costs are similar.

pairs.label: Least connections
pairs.detail: Send new work to the server with fewer active connections.
pairs.explanation: Send new work to the server with fewer active connections. Connection count is useful for long or uneven requests but is still only a proxy for load.

pairs.label: Hash routing
pairs.detail: Hash a declared key when repeat placement is necessary.
pairs.explanation: Hash a declared key when repeat placement is necessary. Choose a key that reflects the real affinity boundary and plan behavior when a server disappears.

pairs.label: Weighted capacity
pairs.detail: Give capable servers proportionally more traffic.
pairs.explanation: Give capable servers proportionally more traffic. Maintain weights as instance shape, limits, and workload change.

Least connections: Send new work to the server with fewer active connections.

Hash routing: Hash a declared key when repeat placement is necessary.

Weighted capacity: Give capable servers proportionally more traffic.

pairs.label: Classify eligibility
pairs.detail: Permit only methods, statuses, routes, and response metadata with a documented shared- cache contract.
pairs.explanation: Permit only methods, statuses, routes, and response metadata with a documented shared- cache contract. Bypass authorization and session-dependent requests by default.

pairs.label: Build the cache key
pairs.detail: Include scheme, host, normalized path/query, and every trusted variation dimension that changes the representation.
pairs.explanation: Include scheme, host, normalized path/query, and every trusted variation dimension that changes the representation.

pairs.label: Define freshness
pairs.detail: Respect application cache headers or an explicit edge policy.
pairs.explanation: Respect application cache headers or an explicit edge policy. Separate freshness from disk inactivity and eviction.

pairs.label: Control refresh
pairs.detail: Use cache locking, background update, conditional revalidation, and permitted stale serving to contain origin work.
pairs.explanation: Use cache locking, background update, conditional revalidation, and permitted stale serving to contain origin work.

pairs.label: Trusted client identity
pairs.detail: Strip or replace inbound forwarding fields at the first trusted edge.
pairs.explanation: Strip or replace inbound forwarding fields at the first trusted edge. Configure real-IP processing only for explicit load-balancer or proxy networks.

pairs.label: Upstream TLS identity
pairs.detail: When proxying over HTTPS, enable certificate verification, provide trusted CAs, set the expected server name, and test rotation and failure.
pairs.explanation: When proxying over HTTPS, enable certificate verification, provide trusted CAs, set the expected server name, and test rotation and failure.

pairs.label: Bound untrusted input
pairs.detail: Limit header and body size, request rate, connection rate, methods, parse time, and temporary-file use before expensive upstream work begins.
pairs.explanation: Limit header and body size, request rate, connection rate, methods, parse time, and temporary-file use before expensive upstream work begins.

pairs.label: Render and validate
pairs.detail: Generate configuration from reviewed inputs, run syntax validation, and execute route, header, cache, and retry tests against the candidate.
pairs.explanation: Generate configuration from reviewed inputs, run syntax validation, and execute route, header, cache, and retry tests against the candidate.

pairs.label: Reload a small edge set
pairs.detail: Apply the candidate to bounded traffic and watch worker startup, upstream selection, status codes, latency, resource use, and security policy.
pairs.explanation: Apply the candidate to bounded traffic and watch worker startup, upstream selection, status codes, latency, resource use, and security policy.

pairs.label: Observe generation overlap
pairs.detail: Track old workers and long-lived connections.
pairs.explanation: Track old workers and long-lived connections. Confirm memory, file descriptors, and logs remain healthy until the old generation exits.

pairs.label: Promote or roll back
pairs.detail: Expand only when user and upstream outcomes remain inside the release envelope.
pairs.explanation: Expand only when user and upstream outcomes remain inside the release envelope. Restore the prior artifact when a route or policy regresses.
